item.title: Education Minister wishes Deans semi-finalists well
item.description: Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro has extended his best wishes to all secondary schools competing in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans Rugby semi-finals today. Radrodro has commended the players, coaches, teachers, parents, former students and supporters for their commitment throughout the competition.
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Education Aseri Radrodro has extended his best wishes to all secondary schools competing in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans Rugby semi-finals today.

Radrodro has commended the players, coaches, teachers, parents, former students and supporters for their commitment throughout the competition.

He is encouraging players to show discipline, sportsmanship, teamwork and respect both on and off the field while representing their schools with pride.

Radrodro says reaching the semi-finals is already a significant achievement and has urged players to enjoy the experience, respect their opponents and give their best regardless of the result.

He has also called on parents, teachers, former students and supporters to support their teams in a positive and respectful manner.

In the Under-18 semi-finals, Suva Grammar School will take on Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park, while Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Australia commits funding for Police headquarters in Veiuto
item.description: The Australian Government has committed funding for the development of a permanent headquarters for the Fiji Police Force in Veiuto. Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua says the development is important for the Force, which has moved from place to place since its establishment 150 years ago.
item.content:encoded:
The Australian Government has committed funding for the development of a permanent headquarters for the Fiji Police Force in Veiuto.

Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua says the development is important for the Force, which has moved from place to place since its establishment 150 years ago.

He says the Government has finally decided to provide the Fiji Police Force with a permanent location, and the Commissioner of Police and him are pleased with the decision.

He adds they are also working on plans with development partners, particularly Australia.

Naivalurua says he is not privy to the figure at this stage but understands it is a significant amount.

He says discussions on the project took place about a year ago and, strategically, the development is the way forward for the Fiji Police Force.

item.title: Police launch active investigation into severe animal cruelty reports
item.description: SPCA Fiji says Police have launched an active investigation into recent reports of severe animal cruelty, with regional teams mobilised in the area where the alleged offence occurred, as the Society awaits the findings and possible arrests of those responsible. SPCA Fiji says it has formally written to the Assistant Commissioner of Police and other relevant authorities regarding the recent reports
item.content:encoded:
SPCA Fiji says Police have launched an active investigation into recent reports of severe animal cruelty, with regional teams mobilised in the area where the alleged offence occurred, as the Society awaits the findings and possible arrests of those responsible.

SPCA Fiji says it has formally written to the Assistant Commissioner of Police and other relevant authorities regarding the recent reports.

The Society has commended the Fiji Police Force for its swift response and proactive engagement, particularly the office of Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe.

It says Police management immediately mobilised regional teams in the area where the alleged offence occurred and an active investigation is now underway.

SPCA Fiji says it remains in direct communication with Police as inquiries continue.

It says Police are also providing ongoing updates on other pending animal cruelty cases around the country, including prominent cases in Suva and Labasa.

The Society says it is awaiting the findings of these investigations and subsequent legal action, including possible arrests of those responsible.

SPCA Fiji stresses that intentional cruelty to animals is a serious criminal offence under Fijian law.

It says it will continue working with law enforcement agencies, municipal councils and government ministries to ensure perpetrators are held accountable and to create a safer and more compassionate environment for animals in Fiji.

We have sent questions to Police seeking confirmation of the investigation.

item.title: India marks 80th Independence Day
item.description: India is celebrating its 80th Independence Day today , marking 79 years since the country gained independence from British rule on 15th August 1947. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead the celebrations at the Red Fort Complex in Delhi amid patriotic fervour and multi-layer security.
item.content:encoded:
India is celebrating its 80th Independence Day today , marking 79 years since the country gained independence from British rule on 15th August 1947.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lead the celebrations at the Red Fort Complex in Delhi amid patriotic fervour and multi-layer security.

For the first time, the National Song, 'Vande Mataram', will be rendered during the Independence Day celebrations.

Ceremonial events are scheduled to be held at state capitals and other cities and towns across the country, which will include flag-hoisting followed by cultural performances.

The day honours the sacrifices of those who fought for India’s freedom and celebrates the country’s journey since independence.

I ndependence Day is marked with the raising of the Indian national flag, cultural programmes and celebrations across India and by Indian communities around the world.

item.description: Residents of Stage One in Cunningham, opposite the Cunningham Community Post, are living in fear and feeling unsafe in their own neighbourhood after repeated thefts and robberies in the area. item.content:encoded:
Residents of Stage One in Cunningham, opposite the Cunningham Community Post, are living in fear and feeling unsafe in their own neighbourhood after repeated thefts and robberies in the area.

A resident, who wishes to remain anonymous told fijivillage News that her home has been broken into three times, and she now avoids carrying her phone, handbag or money whenever she leaves the house because she fears being robbed.

She says she spends most of the day inside her home with the doors locked until her son returns from work, speaking to neighbours through the window because she is too afraid to go outside.

Insert: Resident on theft issue, 14th Aug 26

Residents say homes have been broken into repeatedly, vehicles parked along the roadside have been targeted and crops, including cassava, have been stolen from plantations.

Another family reported household items, including a refrigerator, mattress, television stand and solar equipment, were stolen.

Residents also say people have been robbed while walking along the road, with the robbers using nearby roads to escape.

They say many of the incidents have been reported to Police, but they are frustrated because they feel there has been little follow-up after the initial reports.

Another resident says thieves entered her home while the family was away and on another occasion while they were sleeping.

She says the repeated thefts forced her to close the family's canteen after business items were stolen.

Residents are now calling on the Government and the Fiji Police Force to increase patrols, particularly at night, and install more streetlights, saying poorly lit roads make it easier for criminals to operate.

An officer at the Cunningham Community Post told fijivillage News that the post is a community-based police facility and is responsible for receiving reports from residents before referring criminal matters to the larger police stations.

The officer says serious criminal cases are referred to the Valelevu and Nabua Police Stations, which are responsible for carrying out investigations.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says officers are expected to take the initial reports and make referrals to the larger police stations.

He says Cunningham is supported by patrols from the Valelevu and Nabua Police Stations.

ACP Vusonilawe says the concerns raised by residents regarding patrols will also be looked into.

He is also urging anyone with complaints about police conduct to contact the Police complaints line on 1681.
